title: Model Rule 1.18: Duties to Prospective Client
propositions: prospective-client status; use and disclosure duties; disqualification framework
limitations: not controlling unless adopted; adopted text and interpretations vary by jurisdiction

title: Formal Opinion 512: Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools
issuing_body: ABA Standing Committee on Ethics and Professional Responsibility
propositions: competence; confidentiality; communication; supervision; candor; fees when lawyers use GAI
limitations: does not create binding nationwide law; addresses GAI generally rather than prospective-client intake specifically

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology
propositions: confabulation; data privacy; information integrity; human-AI configuration; value-chain risks; testing and monitoring
limitations: voluntary and cross-sector; does not state legal-ethics duties

title: AI Companies: Uphold Your Privacy and Confidentiality Commitments
issuing_body: Federal Trade Commission Office of Technology
propositions: AI providers' privacy and confidentiality representations; sensitive customer and end-user data; data-use risk
limitations: not a rule or adjudication and not legal-specific

title: Generative AI Practical Guidance
propositions: application of competence; confidentiality; communication; candor and related duties to GAI and agentic AI
limitations: California-specific; educational guidance rather than legal advice; replaces 2023 version

title: Opinion 24-1
propositions: confidentiality; competence and accuracy; fees; advertising when lawyers use GAI
limitations: expressly advisory and nonbinding; not intake-specific

title: Formal Opinion 2024-5: Generative AI in the Practice of Law
issuing_body: New York City Bar Association Committee on Professional Ethics
propositions: competence; confidentiality; supervision; disclosure and other duties regarding GAI
limitations: scope and legal effect must not be generalized to all New York or U.S. lawyers

title: Legal Ethics Opinion 1901: Reasonable Fees and the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: Virginia State Bar / Supreme Court of Virginia
propositions: reasonable fees when GAI makes work more efficient
limitations: focused on fees; not prospective-client intake; status changed after its 2025 proposal stage

title: Formal Opinion 2025-6: Ethical Issues Affecting Use of AI to Record Transcribe and Summarize Conversations with Clients
issuing_body: New York City Bar Association Committee on Professional Ethics
propositions: consent; tactical assessment; confidentiality and privilege; accuracy checking for preserved AI summaries
limitations: concerns client conversations rather than web-form prospective-client intake; analogy must be labeled

title: Formal Opinion 510: Avoiding Imputation of a Conflict of Interest When a Law Firm Is Adverse to One of Its Lawyer's Prospective Clients
issuing_body: ABA Standing Committee on Ethics and Professional Responsibility
limitations: not an AI opinion; full opinion and precise application require acquisition and pinpoint review
